messages.text: Una ruta en 3D en la Alhambra de Granada en un solo fichero html Guarda lo que generes en la carpeta actual.

content.text:
The user wants a 3D tour of the Alhambra in Granada in a single HTML file, saved to the current working directory. I should create an interactive 3D scene using Three.js (via CDN, since it needs to be a single file). Let me think about what to build: - A 3D representation of the Alhambra complex: the Nasrid Palaces (Mexuar, Comares/Patio de los Arrayanes, Patio de los Leones), the Alcazaba, the Palace of Charles V, the Generalife gardens perhaps. - A "ruta" (route/tour) - so a walking path through the sites, with waypoints, camera animations, points of interest with info panels. - Single HTML file with Three.js from CDN. I should build: 1. Ground/terrain with the Sabika hill 2. Alcazaba (towers: Torre de la Vela, etc.) 3. Nasrid Palaces with courtyards (Patio de los Arrayanes with pool, Patio de los Leones with fountain and lion statues simplified) 4. Palace of Charles V (circular building with square interior — actually circular exterior with circular courtyard) 5. Generalife with gardens 6. Torres Bermejas maybe 7. A route path with markers (numbered stops), clickable to fly camera to each stop 8. UI: route list panel, info about each stop, play tour button, controls (orbit, pan, zoom) 9. Day/night lighting maybe, sun 10. Trees (cypresses), water features Text in Spanish since user speaks Spanish. I'll use Three.js r160+ via CDN (unpkg or jsdelivr) with ES modules via importmap. Need to be careful: CDN modules work when file is opened directly? ES modules from CDN work over https from a local file — yes, since the script tag imports from https URL, CORS is allowed by CDN. That works with file://? Import maps and module scripts from remote origins do work in modern browsers even when the page is file://... Actually module scripts from https CDN loaded from file:// page: the page origin is "null", but CDN sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so it works. Yes, this generally works. To be safe, I could use the non-module build (three.min.js UMD) but newer three versions dropped UMD builds (after r150 or so they warn; r160 removed three.js UMD? The UMD build was removed in r160? Actually the "build/three.js" UMD was deprecated and removed in r160; three.module.js remains). I can use an importmap with jsdelivr: ```html ``` Then import OrbitControls from three/addons. I'll write good geometry: - Ground plane with hill (maybe use a big plane, with the complex on a plateau) - Walls around the complex, crenellations - Towers: Torre de la Vela, various towers as cylinders/boxes with battlements - Puerta de la Justicia (gate) - Palacio de Comares: rectangular courtyard (Patio de los Arrayanes) with long pool, Salón de Comares with tower (Torre de Comares) - Patio de los Leones: square courtyard, central fountain with 12 lions (simplified: small cylinders), arcades with columns (instanced columns), Salón de los Abencerrajes and Salón de los Reyes with domes - Mexuar: simpler building - Palacio de Carlos V: circular ring building with circular courtyard, two-story with columned arcades - Generalife: separate with long pool (Patio de la Acequia), gardens, trees - Water: pools with animated water material, small channels (acequias) - Trees: cypress cones, orange trees maybe - Sky: gradient sky, sun, clouds optional - Route: a spline path on the ground with markers (numbered billboards). Camera flies between stops with smooth interpolation. Info panel with title, description of each stop. - UI: header, side list with buttons for each stop, "Reproducir ruta" / "Detener", previous/next, maybe a minimap? Minimap might be too much. Keep: route panel + info + controls hint. - Also free exploration with OrbitControls. - Points of interest as clickable objects (raycasting) - maybe simpler: click list items. Stops for the route (realistic order): 1. Puerta de la Justicia (entrance) 2. Alcazaba y Torre de la Vela 3. Palacio de Carlos V 4. Mexuar 5. Patio de los Arrayanes (Palacio de Comares) & Salón de Comares 6. Patio de los Leones 7. Generalife (via walk, cross hill) 8. Torre Bermeja viewpoint / end I'll write the code carefully so it runs without errors. Key considerations: - Use InstancedMesh for columns and battlements for performance. - Use BufferGeometry merge where handy, or just individual meshes (counts are moderate). - Shadows: enable directional light shadows with decent shadow map size. - Water animation: simple sine displacement in vertex shader? Could do a simple ShaderMaterial with time uniform. Or use MeshPhongMaterial with normal offset... Simplest: custom ShaderMaterial with animated normals/waves. Or use three's Water from examples (addons/objects/Water.js) — needs textures from CDN; Water requires a normals texture from three examples repo: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/waternormals.jpg — that's fetchable. But cross-origin texture loading works with CORS. Could be risky if offline; but the whole thing needs CDN anyway. I'll write a simple custom water shader instead to reduce external deps beyond the core module. Actually simple animated water: ShaderMaterial with fresnel + moving pseudo-waves via sin functions in fragment. That's doable without textures. - Text sprites for stop markers: use CanvasTexture with numbers. - Camera fly: implement with easing between stop positions; use a class TourController. - Path line: CatmullRomCurve3 through waypoints, TubeGeometry or line with dots. I'll draw a dashed/arrowed path: small spheres along curve plus a Line. ## Qué incluye

**Ruta guiada de 9 paradas** con vuelos de cámara cinematográficos y narración histórica:
1. Puerta de la Justicia (1348) → 2. Alcazaba y Torre de la Vela → 3. Plaza de los Aljibes (Washington Irving) → 4. Mexuar → 5. Patio de los Arrayanes → 6. Salón de los Embajadores (torre de Comares) → 7. Patio de los Leones con la fuente de los 12 leones → 8. Palacio de Carlos V → 9. Generalife

**Escena 3D estilizada** construida con three.js: murallas con almenas, la Alcazaba con su campana, los palacios nazaríes con patios huecos, columnas y arcos de medio punto instanciados, el anillo circular renacentista, el Generalife con su Patio de la Acequia, surtidores de agua animados con shader propio, la Escalera del Agua, la ciudad de Granada y el Albaicín al fondo, la vega y Sierra Nevada nevada con niebla atmosférica y nubes en movimiento.

**Interacción**: línea dorada con flechas y caminantes que recorren el itinerario real (subiendo la Cuesta de Gomérez y atravesando las salas-pasaje), marcadores numerados clicables, panel de itinerario, botones de reproducir/pausa/anterior/siguiente, vista aérea, control orbital libre (arrastrar, rueda, clic derecho) y atajos de teclado (← → espacio).
